barriers.reason: The patient cannot drive after stroke, her only driver (daughter) works 7–5 and cannot bring her to 9 AM MWF appointments, and she is not steady enough to use the bus with a walker from 111th, so three weekly trips to the rehab center are not reliably feasible as written.

alternatives.text: If the patient has Medicaid or dual coverage, arrange non-emergency medical transport through her managed care plan (call the number on the plan card) or Transdev for fee-for-service, booked in advance for the standing MWF therapy trips.
Ask the hospital rehab center for a later chair/therapy start time or different days that fall when the daughter is off work, framing it as a scheduling request given limited chair times.

If her condition prevents using CTA/Pace fixed-route buses and trains, apply for ADA Paratransit certification (Northern Illinois Transit Authority, 312-663-HELP); note it is not immediate and runs only when fixed-route service operates.

barriers.reason: The single neurology follow-up requires travel the patient cannot provide herself (cannot drive; daughter works 7–5; bus with walker is not manageable), so getting to that appointment is uncertain unless a ride is arranged.

alternatives.text: Check coverage: if Medicaid/dual, book a one-way ride via the plan's NEMT line or Transdev; if Medicare-only, check whether a Medicare Advantage plan includes a transportation benefit before promising a covered ride.
Schedule the follow-up on a day/time that matches a family member's availability or coordinate it with another existing trip to reduce separate travel.
Consider whether any part of the neurology follow-up can be done by telehealth if no in-person exam is needed, removing the transport barrier entirely.
